chunks: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

If you intend to depart in two days, then you may not depart until the sun passes the zenith. But if you delay until the last of the days of Tashrīq, which is the final day of departure, then there is no issue upon you whatever hour you depart, and you threw the pebbles before the zenith or after it.

key_terms.أَيَّامِ التَّشْرِيقِ: the designated post-Eid days in hajj
key_terms.تَزُولَ الشَّمْسُ: the sun passing the zenith; the time after midday
key_terms.تَنْفِرَ: to depart from Minā during hajj rites
key_terms.رَمَيْتَ: you performed the throwing of pebbles at the jamarāt
key_terms.يَوْمُ النَّفْرِ الْأَخِيرِ: the final day of departure from Minā

ai.seo_question: When is it permissible to depart from Minā during the days of Tashrīq?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning departure from Minā during the days of Tashrīq in hajj. It states that one intending to leave on the second day must wait until after zawāl, while one who remains until the final day of departure may leave at any time, whether the stoning is done before or after zawāl.
